security_audit.summary: SKILL.md is a single 31-line Markdown documentation file with no executable code. All 10 static findings flagged Markdown inline-code backticks around file paths and identifiers as Ruby/shell backtick execution; every one is a false positive, as backticks in Markdown are formatting, not command execution. No network calls, no scripts, no environment access, and no prompt-injection or data-exfiltration intent were found.

remediation.issue: Static analyzer misclassified Markdown inline-code backticks as shell/Ruby command execution.
remediation.suggestion: No action required from the author. The backticks are standard Markdown formatting around file names and identifiers. If the pattern rule is tunable, exclude Markdown code spans from backtick-execution detection.

finding_verdicts.reason: The backticks wrap the Markdown inline-code path `backend/ingest.py` in a documentation bullet. This is Markdown formatting, not shell or Ruby backtick execution, and the file contains no interpreter that would evaluate it.
The backticks wrap the directory name `docs/` as inline code inside a prose description of the ingestion process. No command is executed; it is a Markdown code span.
The backticks wrap the embedding model identifier `models/text-embedding-004` as inline code. This is documentation text, not backtick command execution.
The backticks wrap the Qdrant collection name `physical_ai_book` as inline code in a numbered list. No shell or Ruby evaluation occurs in a Markdown file.

The backticks wrap the documented run command `python backend/ingest.py`. It is a usage note shown to the reader as inline code, not an instruction the skill itself executes; there is no runtime that would run it.
The backticks wrap the client library name `qdrant-client` as inline code. This is a Markdown code span, not backtick execution.
The backticks wrap the collection name `physical_ai_book` as inline code. Pure documentation formatting with no executable semantics.
The backticks wrap the file path `backend/utils/helpers.py` as inline code. This is a Markdown reference, not a shell or Ruby backtick command.
The backticks wrap file paths and field names (`backend/personalization.py`, `software_background`) as inline code within prose. No command execution is present in this Markdown file.
The backticks wrap the class name `Agent` and file path `backend/agents.py` as inline code describing an agentic wrapper. This is documentation, not backtick command execution.

content.user_title: Document a Retrieval Augmented Generation Pipeline
content.value_statement: Understanding how a RAG system moves from raw documents to grounded answers is hard when the ingestion, vector search, and prompt steps live in separate files. This skill gives an AI assistant a concise map of the whole pipeline so it can explain, extend, or debug each stage with accurate context.
actual_capabilities: Explains the document ingestion flow: scanning a docs directory, cleaning MDX, chunking, embedding, and upserting.
Documents the Qdrant vector search setup, including collection name, vector size, and cosine similarity.
Describes how RAG prompts are constructed from retrieved context chunks.
Outlines personalization logic that tailors system instructions to user background fields.
Summarizes an agentic wrapper class that wraps LLM calls for future multi-agent expansion.
limitations: Provides documentation only; it contains no runnable code or scripts.
References external files such as backend/ingest.py that are not included in the skill.
Assumes a specific stack (Qdrant, text-embedding-004) and does not cover alternatives.
Does not include configuration, credentials, or deployment instructions.

use_cases.title: Onboard a new engineer to the pipeline
use_cases.description: A developer joining the project uses the skill to quickly understand each stage of the RAG pipeline before reading the source code.

use_cases.title: Extend the ingestion or search logic
use_cases.description: An engineer plans a change to chunking or the vector collection and relies on the documented settings to keep behavior consistent.

use_cases.title: Explain the system to stakeholders
use_cases.description: A technical lead uses the summary to describe how retrieval and personalization work without walking through code.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize the pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Using the RAG Pipeline skill, give me a plain-language summary of how a document becomes a searchable answer.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a single stage
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the ingestion stage of this RAG pipeline step by step, including chunk size and the embedding model used.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a change
prompt_templates.prompt: I want to change the chunk size and overlap in the ingestion process. Based on the documented pipeline, what should I check before making this change?

prompt_templates.title: Design an extension
prompt_templates.prompt: Using the documented Agent class and vector search setup, propose a design for adding a re-ranking step before prompt construction.

output_examples.input: Give me a plain-language summary of this RAG pipeline.
output_examples.output: The pipeline scans a documents folder, cleans and chunks the text, turns each chunk into a numeric embedding, and stores those in a Qdrant collection. At query time it finds the most similar chunks using cosine similarity, builds a prompt that includes that retrieved context, and personalizes the system instructions based on the user's background before sending the request to the language model.

output_examples.input: What similarity metric and vector size does the search use?
output_examples.output: The Qdrant collection uses a vector size of 768, matching the Gecko-004 embedding output, and compares vectors using cosine similarity.

best_practices: Keep the documented settings such as chunk size, vector size, and collection name in sync with the actual backend code.
Use the skill to orient before editing pipeline files, then confirm details against the source.
Reference the personalization fields when tailoring answers to a specific user profile.
anti_patterns: Treating the skill as executable code; it is documentation and runs nothing on its own.
Assuming the referenced backend files are bundled with the skill.
Changing chunk size or vector size in one place without updating the pipeline end to end.

faq.question: Does this skill run any code or commands?
faq.answer: No. It is a single Markdown documentation file. The backticks it contains are formatting around file names and identifiers, not commands.

faq.question: What vector database does the pipeline use?
faq.answer: It uses Qdrant, with a collection named physical_ai_book and cosine similarity.

faq.question: What embedding model is documented?
faq.answer: The pipeline embeds text with models/text-embedding-004, producing 768-dimensional vectors.

faq.question: How is text chunked before embedding?
faq.answer: Text is chunked into roughly 1000-character segments with a 100-character overlap after MDX cleaning.

faq.question: How does personalization work?
faq.answer: A personalization step builds system instructions using the user's software_background and hardware_background fields.

faq.question: Can I use this skill to modify the pipeline directly?
faq.answer: It helps you understand and plan changes, but the actual edits must be made in the referenced backend source files, which are not part of the skill.
